extracted.intended_audience: media lawyers, news-agency managers, judges, and scholars of press/publishing law
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and operational standards governing when and how one news agency may (or may not) use, copy, or resell news gathered by another agency, and the equitable remedies (injunctions) available for misappropriation. Focuses on confidentiality, permissible uses of published items, agency liability, and the 'unclean hands' equitable defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of agency news until publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The news collected by [an agency] and transmitted to its subscribers 'shall remain confidential and secret until publication thereof has been fully accomplished by the subscriber to whom it is so furnished.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confidentiality is breached before the subscriber publishes, competitors could obtain and use the news without expense, thereby seriously impairing the value and utility of the original agency's service. Protection of pre-publication secrecy is essential to the business model.

rubrics_metrics.name: By‑laws/contractual limits on member use
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are contractually bound (by certificates/by‑laws) to receive AP service 'for the purpose of publication in the newspaper specified in his certificate of membership and for that purpose only' and 'shall not furnish or permit any one ... to furnish to any person who is not a member news of The Associated Press in advance of publication.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These by‑laws impose obligations on members (e.g., to publish AP news only in specified paper/language/place and to supply local news to AP and to no one else) and form the basis for claims when members supply pre‑publication news to rivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value criterion: accuracy and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of news accumulated by a news agency 'depends upon its accuracy and upon its reaching the newspapers served before the news of any other competing news agency can be furnished.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both accuracy and delivery timing are core metrics of a news service's value; misappropriation that defeats either element (e.g., by prematurely conveying the item to rivals) harms the agency's business and supports relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of prompt publication and cooperative collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt knowledge and publication of world‑wide news is essential to modern newspapers, and because of the 'enormous expense' of gathering such news, proprietors obtain it either by cooperation (sharing expense) or by purchase from an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This grounds recognition that news agencies' systems (and protections for their outputs) are commercially necessary to sustain wide reporting; it contextualizes why courts protect agency news from abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited practice A: hiring member employees to furnish pre‑publication news
rubrics_metrics.description: It is wrongful to arrange with employees of members of a rival news service to furnish that rival's news to you 'as soon as the same was received, and prior to its publication' (i.e., obtaining pre‑publication tips from member employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic hiring/arrangements (even at modest pay) to obtain pre‑publication news from members supports injunctive relief; such acts violate contractual duties and are actionable regardless of whether the rival agency's managers knew of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited practice B: inducing members to violate by‑laws to grant early access
rubrics_metrics.description: Inducing members to violate their association by‑laws (permitting a non‑member to obtain news before publication) is wrongful and actionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liability lies where a rival causes or entices a member to break contractual obligations that protect an agency's pre‑publication exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited practice C: copying from bulletin boards/early editions and selling without verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Copying news from bulletin boards or from early editions of a rival's member newspapers and selling this news to customers (in the same text or paraphrase) without independent verification is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a distinction between reading competitors' early editions to learn a rumor and then independently verifying (permissible) versus republishing or transmitting stories based on those early editions without independent investigation (improper and not recognized as fair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use: rumor/tip followed by independent investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking a newspaper item for the mere information or rumor that an event has happened is permissible provided the receiving agency 'proceeds to obtain the news by its own independent investigation from the original sources at its own expense' and transmits only a story based 'solely upon the strength of such investigation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common practice among agencies; acceptable so long as the final dispatch is based on independent verification rather than on the rival's text or details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible use: sending out story based on rival's copy without investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sending out a story 'based in whole or in part upon the news obtained from the newspaper without independent investigation' (including sending the bare statement of fact or extended copy of the rival's details) is unfair and improper and has not been recognized or allowed by AP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission that relies on the competitor's published text or details without verification is actionable appropriation; agencies should avoid reproducing or paraphrasing competitor copy as their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal liability for acts within scope of employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts done by persons 'acting for [a defendant] within the general scope of their employment' (e.g., employees who obtain pre‑publication news or copy sheets) render the principal liable; liability rests upon the principal irrespective of its officers' knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if upper management claims ignorance, systematic or frequent acts by employees within their employment scope can establish the corporation's liability and justify injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable defense ('unclean hands') requires principal's knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: To bar relief in equity on the ground that the complainant has acted unconscionably ('he who comes into equity must come in with clear hands'), there must be evidence of knowledge on the part of those exercising general control over the complainant's affairs; mere imputations or technical agency theories are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolated or sporadic lapses by lower employees, not shown to have been known or ratified by controlling officers, will not necessarily deprive a complainant of equitable relief; the defense requires more than allegations of sporadic misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic appropriation vs. sporadic lapses
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic, continuous appropriation of a rival's news (e.g., habitual procurement of pre‑publication tips, copying by assaulting bulletin boards, or surreptitious wire‑tapping) is materially different from occasional or sporadic lapses and supports stronger judicial relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will weigh frequency, systematization, and secrecy (e.g., secret employment for the purpose) when determining wrongful appropriation vs. inevitable occasional mistakes in news work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and meaning of 'tip' for news use
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever the word 'tip' is used it 'shall be deemed to connote information of a news event so outlining the main features of that event as to enable the person to whom it is given to identify the event, and to locate the place of its origin, thus enabling verification or amplification thereof.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'tip' contains sufficient identifying features to permit verification; receiving a tip creates the obligation to verify by independent investigation before publication as one's own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against sale to later‑publishing regions (time‑zone withholding)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical part of a countrywide news agency's operation is to prevent rivals from selling news published by its Eastern members to Western newspapers (published later) so that the rivals cannot undercut the agency's investment by selling the same news at no collection cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time/territory‑based protection of news helps preserve the agency's labor value; improper early disclosure that enables such resale can be enjoined.
